title: Vibe Coding Foundations
description: Understand what vibe coding is, where it helps, where it fails, and the engineering mindset that keeps speed from becoming fragility.

lessons.title: Vibe coding is an interaction style
lessons.principle: AI-assisted development uses conversational intent, examples, and feedback loops to produce and revise software.
lessons.practice: Use natural-language direction for speed, but keep explicit requirements, review, and verification around the generated code.

lessons.title: Speed is not the same as correctness
lessons.principle: Fast generation reduces typing time, not the need to establish whether behavior is correct.
lessons.practice: Measure success by verified outcomes, maintainability, and user impact rather than by how quickly code appears.

lessons.title: The model is a collaborator, not an authority
lessons.principle: Coding models can synthesize useful implementations while still misunderstanding requirements or inventing details.
lessons.practice: Treat every generated change as a proposal that must survive inspection, tests, and domain checks.

lessons.title: Know when not to vibe code
lessons.principle: High-risk domains, ambiguous requirements, irreversible data changes, and security-critical paths demand stronger controls.
lessons.practice: Increase specification, review depth, testing, and specialist involvement as consequence and uncertainty rise.

lessons.title: Own the final code
lessons.principle: The developer remains responsible for code merged, deployed, and operated regardless of who or what generated it.
lessons.practice: Do not merge code you cannot explain well enough to debug, review, or safely modify.

lessons.title: Use a risk-based workflow
lessons.principle: Different tasks deserve different levels of autonomy and verification.
lessons.practice: Classify changes by blast radius, data sensitivity, reversibility, and user impact before choosing an AI workflow.

lessons.title: Prefer small reversible increments
lessons.principle: Small changes make intent, review, rollback, and debugging easier.
lessons.practice: Ask for one coherent slice at a time and keep each change independently testable and revertible.

lessons.title: Preserve causality
lessons.principle: Understanding what changed and why is essential when AI can generate large diffs quickly.
lessons.practice: Keep commits focused and record the rationale behind architectural or behavioral decisions.

lessons.title: Make hidden assumptions explicit
lessons.principle: Models often fill gaps with defaults that may not match the product or codebase.
lessons.practice: Ask the agent to list assumptions and convert important ones into requirements or tests.

lessons.title: Separate exploration from production
lessons.principle: Prototypes optimize learning; production code optimizes reliable operation.
lessons.practice: Label experiments clearly and deliberately harden only the approaches that survive validation.

lessons.title: Use the computer as an evidence source
lessons.principle: Repository files, tests, logs, type errors, and runtime behavior are more trustworthy than model confidence.
lessons.practice: Ask agents to inspect real artifacts and run checks instead of reasoning from memory when evidence is available.

lessons.title: Iteration beats one-shot prompting
lessons.principle: Complex software rarely emerges correctly from a single prompt.
lessons.practice: Use inspect-plan-implement-verify-review cycles and refine based on observed results.

lessons.title: Constrain before accelerating
lessons.principle: Clear boundaries reduce accidental scope expansion and incompatible design choices.
lessons.practice: State what must not change, what APIs are stable, and what files or systems are out of scope.

lessons.title: Optimize for understanding
lessons.principle: A codebase that only the model can navigate is an operational risk.
lessons.practice: Keep naming, module boundaries, tests, and documentation legible to humans.

lessons.title: Treat generated volume as review debt
lessons.principle: Large outputs can overwhelm human attention and hide subtle defects.
lessons.practice: Limit diff size, split work, and require summaries of behavior-changing edits.

lessons.title: Feedback quality determines output quality
lessons.principle: Models improve when they receive precise error messages, diffs, examples, and acceptance failures.
lessons.practice: Feed concrete evidence back into the next iteration rather than saying only that something is wrong.

lessons.title: Automate objective checks
lessons.principle: Machines are better than memory at repeatedly enforcing syntax, tests, types, linting, and policy.
lessons.practice: Make reliable checks cheap and automatic so fast iteration does not erode standards.

lessons.title: Retain human judgment
lessons.principle: Product tradeoffs, ethical choices, architecture, and ambiguous user needs still require accountable judgment.
lessons.practice: Use AI to expand options and analysis, then make consequential decisions deliberately.

lessons.title: Know your stop condition
lessons.principle: Unbounded prompting can create churn and regressions.
lessons.practice: Define done as acceptance criteria satisfied, validations green, diff reviewed, and risks understood.

lessons.title: Vibe coding should mature into engineering
lessons.principle: The strongest workflow combines conversational velocity with disciplined software delivery.
lessons.practice: Use AI to compress low-value effort while strengthening specifications, tests, review, and operational readiness.

codeExamples.snippet:
Risk: medium
Goal: ship a reversible change
Evidence:
- focused tests pass
- final diff reviewed
- rollback path known

git diff --check
npm test
npm run build
